links.comparator_used: Unprotected Med42-v2-8B with no privacy-preserving method
links.outcome: Privacy leakage rate and clinical utility score (1-5) in medical open-ended QA
links.effect: Leakage fell from 72.8% to 20.5% with local differential privacy, but utility fell from 3.87/5 to 3.03
links.tradeoff: Large utility loss: the lowest leakage came with a drop in utility from 3.87 to 3.03. The authors describe a pervasive privacy-utility trade-off.
links.quote: Relative to unprotected Med42-v2-8B (utility 3.87/5; leakage 72.8%), supervised fine-tuning improved utility to 4.25 and reduced leakage to 38.9%, whereas local differential privacy reduced leakage to 20.5% but lowered utility to 3.03.

design_hint: privacy-preserving methods (differential privacy and fine-tuning guardrails against contextual leakage)
